units: Execution adapters are distinct from the 3 newly registered TOOL/WORKER contracts. Multiple launch sites may share one adapter; parsing/cleanup offloads are not new business authorities.

entries.revalidation: Stable owner and enqueue epoch; immutable entire job/item plan before each file and before commit; actual source permit tied to active transaction and actual TransformResult; domain locks before final actor SHARE.

entries.authority: Legacy producer only; no stable canonical owner/epoch/manifest.
entries.revalidation: Each file reads only actual input bytes to identify its source, then acquires shared transaction cutover lock before business locks. First activation takes exclusive lock until marker commit. Unknown source guards all five; different never-cutover source retains compatibility.
entries.legacy_residual: Must remain executable only while actual source is never cut over, including worker execution/commit; queue-time check alone is insufficient.

entries.trigger: FastAPI BackgroundTasks from submit and retry
entries.authority: Actual persisted submit/retry producer contract, complete original targets, generation and stable owner; not a newly invented WORKER permission.
entries.revalidation: Wrapper now selects only batch ID/owner/protocol. Protected worker restores identity and validates actual sidecar/provenance before bytes, then revalidates after all domain writes before commit. Expired epoch/revoked Grant leaves queued state and zero raw/plan/receipts. Legacy processing/write/failure-publication transactions each begin with the shared cutover guard; no stale failure report after activation.
entries.legacy_residual: No-owner legacy can run only before resource authority; after cutover it reaches protected reader and fails closed.

entries.authority: agent_chat.use AND private_chat_session.run; actual session self ownership. Every tool separately requires its actual resource actions. Execution permissions are not persisted as content sources.
entries.revalidation: Typed AgentAccess through runtime/dispatch, LLM chunk/publication and checkpoint checks; actual source collector; terminal authorization error stops checkpoint/final answer. Hub attach and persisted history independently revalidate current reader. Legacy short writes acquire a global canonical-management transition shared transaction lock before domain/user locks; every first resource marker or artifact-protocol marker takes matching exclusive lock. No lock spans LLM/formatting. Session create/rename/delete/append/checkpoint share this guarded write boundary; legacy generated bytes/meta use exclusive file creation plus complete temporary metadata hardlink under the same short transaction, cleaning only this candidate on failure.
entries.legacy_residual: Only while canonical_management_required is false, observed under the shared global transition barrier. Process configuration changes require deployment process coordination and are not claimed to be atomic database events.

entries.authority: Exact project-workbook validate HTTP contract; complete document fields and actual project, input hash, stable actor.
entries.revalidation: Canonical worker uses its own session, typed identity, complete document/parent proof and final current authorization. Legacy-only worker acquires the shared resource cutover transaction guard as the first database operation before adapter construction or business reads. Project cleanup keeps its original independent transaction; commit or rollback is followed by a second guard before the actual validation transaction.
entries.legacy_residual: Legacy helpers remain solely for never-cutover request branch; no reuse of username as canonical identity.

entries.authority: maintenance_manager_workbook exact validate, actual owner and full current primary-manager project set; whole-document field contract.
entries.revalidation: Canonical worker uses its own session, typed identity, complete document/parent proof and final current authorization. Legacy-only worker acquires the shared resource cutover transaction guard as the first database operation before adapter construction or business reads. The guard remains held through the original validation transaction commit or rollback.
entries.legacy_residual: Legacy thread path only never-cutover; runtime cannot downgrade a persisted cutover to old role.

entries.authority: maintenance_cost_roundtrip exact input/wholefile contract; worker resumes stable user ID and epoch.
entries.revalidation: Canonical path resumes stable owner+epoch and complete current input/targets. Legacy canonical=None now guards first in its own Session and holds the resource shared transaction lock through actual import commit/rollback; no authorization object is fabricated.
entries.legacy_residual: Old mode only while never-cutover; queued/inflight legacy execution serialized with first activation.

entries.authority: maintenance_warehouse_import preview/apply exact input or persisted receipt branch; actual recursive parent closure.
entries.revalidation: Canonical facade owns exact proof and final domain-to-actor sequence. Legacy _apply_worker now calls resource shared transaction guard as its first database operation, holding it through real apply commit/rollback; first activation waits.
entries.legacy_residual: Only genuinely never-cutover old branch; queued or inflight crossing serialized with activation.

entries.trigger: run_in_threadpool; callers checklist, doc, CKD, ledger, AI fallback
entries.authority: No independent data authority; parsing actual request bytes only. Actual storing/LLM/business projection remains behind producer's exact domain authorization.
entries.revalidation: Input parsing does not query stored business facts or create grants; typed facade rechecks input digest and actual target metadata before persistence/external LLM.
entries.legacy_residual: Shared content parser, not an old permission truth source.

entries.authority: Actual materialized document/source ResourceAccess lineage, not owner/admin bypass.
entries.revalidation: Complete spool already materialized in authorized RR snapshot; current reader/provenance before headers and each bounded chunk; closes on cancellation/failure.
entries.legacy_residual: New canonical publisher only; old unbound generated files fail closed.

entries.authority: Exact dashboard export ResourceAccess and complete field projection.
entries.revalidation: Current lineage before headers and chunks; no new facts read outside original materialized snapshot.
entries.legacy_residual: Explicit canonical export wrapper, not a new worker scope.

entries.trigger: run_in_threadpool after failed formal request; skipped authorization views
entries.authority: Fixed security audit effect even for rejected requests; no business write authority.
entries.revalidation: Revalidates named actor only for audit attribution; records safe status/method/validated UUID, never request body/token/exception. Independent audit transaction intentionally persists denial.
entries.legacy_residual: Shared defensive audit, not permission fallback.

entries.trigger: asyncio.create_task for form close and temp-file spool
entries.authority: Request-owned temporary bytes only; no business facts, archive ownership or authorization decision.
entries.revalidation: Cancellation waits for save/close terminal state; only owned temp unlinked and limiter released after worker terminal.
entries.legacy_residual: Required resource lifetime code shared by both modes.

entries.authority: No independent authority; exact typed caller callback owns domain session and checks.
entries.revalidation: Defers repeated cancellation until worker terminal; propagates original failure; never cancels authorization checks or prematurely unlinks input.
entries.legacy_residual: Generic execution helper; no legacy policy lookup.

limits: Daemon threads are process-local. Durable crash recovery/requeue is not implemented or claimed by this migration.
Offline operator scripts with direct DATABASE_URL access are separately enumerated; employee Grants cannot constrain a trusted database operator. They are not HTTP/Agent-authorized endpoints.
Framework-internal threadpool dispatch of synchronous FastAPI handlers is covered by the actual HTTP entry contract, not counted again as a worker.
Launch-site discovery is structural evidence. Persistent tests and explicit open findings determine semantic closure.
